target_customer: Multi-location restaurants, retailers and other businesses wanting on-the-spot customer feedback
problem: Businesses lacked cheap point of sale feedback and relied on web surveys.
business_model: Enterprise subscription licensing of tablet hardware and analytics

founders.name: D. Scott Phoenix
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder and CEO; TechCrunch Oct 2008 names the CEO as Scott Brown, a conflict.

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom firmware on the Nokia N810 tablet plus analytics software, hardware dependent.

defensibility.rationale: Off the shelf tablet and survey logic, though Google as an early customer was a reference.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; HappyOrNot launched in 2009 and later grew widely.

market_need_then: Pilots in restaurants, stores, trade shows and offices, and Google signed as first large customer after months of pilots (TechCrunch Oct 2008).

brand_strength.rationale: TechCrunch shows a logo but gives no brand detail; no community or press about the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Frogmetrics showed an early traction signal when Google became its first large customer after pilots in 2008, using custom firmware on the Nokia N810 tablet. After that no coverage, round or exit surfaced, so the reason it later became inactive is not public. Its website domain no longer resolves from this environment.
notes: Website did not resolve (DNS not found), treated as dead or blocked. CB Insights says $20K over 2 rounds with investors listed, one seed on 2008-06-26; only the single database, so the amount is left null and total is unverified. Seedtable lists Weston Gaddy as founder, conflicting with YC; not used. Competitors empty: HappyOrNot started in 2009 and the TechCrunch article names none.
